why_this_file_exists: The audit-preservation gate (ADR-042) exists so that a change to src/omi/ cannot move a
previously-reported number silently. ADR-061 changes the observed/inferred CRITERION, which
is an approved change to what a label means -- so some label-valued observations must move,
and a gate that forbade all movement would either block an approved change or be switched
off, which is worse than either.
This file is the third option: every moved observation is enumerated in advance with its
before and after values and its reason. The gate reports declared movements separately and
still FAILS on any undeclared one, so the property it protects -- nothing changes silently
The gate additionally REFUSES an exception whose before or after value is numeric. That is
the mechanical form of the claim this change rests on: ADR-061 alters a label, not a
computed quantity. An attempt to except a number would fail the gate rather than pass it.

changed.name: contrast_label_set
changed.reason: ADR-061. At time_index 0 with the framework default window of 0, contrast's declared suite has no near-diagonal observation, so a direction carrying no Gramian information has an undefined dominance ratio. Spec 3.3's 'inferred' requires identifiability FROM THE TOTAL, which such a direction lacks; the superseded criterion swept it into `inferred` through its else-branch.

changed.name: old_target_labels
changed.reason: ADR-061. Three of flagship's four previously-`inferred` directions carry no observational information at all and now abstain. The two whose danger scores were largest are among them -- the correction that matters, recorded in E-55.

changed.name: new_target_labels
changed.reason: ADR-061, same as old_target_labels. That the two lists still agree is the point of the test that records them (ADR-037's re-run check): adding `bend_angle` to the target set does not reorder the triage, and that remains true under the corrected criterion.

retired.name: contrast_inferred_directions_danger_scores
retired.reason: A NUMERIC observation whose value is a label-filtered list. Its numbers did not move -- every per-direction danger score is byte-identical -- but the filter selecting them changed, so the list would have. Retired under its old name and reissued under a new one rather than silently reusing a name whose meaning changed. Reusing it would have been the only way this change could have moved a number while appearing not to.

retired.name: flagship_inferred_directions_danger_scores
retired.reason: Same, and this is the sharpest single piece of evidence for E-55: the two largest values here, 8.00 and 4.31, belong to directions that carry NO observational information and are now `unresolved`. Under the superseded criterion the framework's own differentiator -- 'what no tabular baseline can recover' -- was carried on flagship by its two highest-danger directions, neither of which any instrument or chain informs at all.
